title: City Life
objectives: Read and spell each syllable, then put them together to read or spell the whole word
Use clues from the sentence to guess what a new word means
Write a simple sentence with a subject and a matching verb
Speed up when a text is easier or when I am reading for fun
Follow and give directions on a map
Fill in a planning tool with ideas before I start writing

sentences.text: Hessa, how do I get to your house?
Walk straight between the library and the mosque.
When you reach the corner, turn left.
Walk past the park, then cross the road.
My house is the villa opposite the library.
Great! Now we can visit each other.

grammar.title: Giving directions
explain: Directions tell someone how to get to a place.
Go straight. Turn left. Turn right. Cross the road.
Walk past the park. It is opposite the library. It is between the mall and the mosque.
examples: The library is opposite the park.

practice.prompt: Walk ___ the park. (go by it without stopping)
My house is ___ the library. (on the other side, facing it)
Look both ways, then ___ the road.

grammar.title: Syllables in long words
explain: Long words are made of small parts called syllables.
Read or spell one syllable at a time, then put them together.

grammar.title: She walks / They walk
explain: Match the verb to the subject.
He, she, it or one person: add -s → Hessa walks to school.
I, you, we, they: no -s → We walk to the park.
examples: The bus stops at the mall.

practice.prompt: We ___ to the park on Friday.

reading.title: The Library Book
paragraphs: Khalid has a library book. He must take it back today. But Khalid is new in the city, and he doesn't know the way.
Grandma draws a map for him. "Go straight along our road," she says. "Walk past the supermarket and the cinema. At the corner, turn right."
Khalid follows the map. He walks past the busy supermarket. He walks past the cinema. At the corner, he turns right. He sees a big park with a fountain.

"The library is opposite the park," Grandma said. Khalid looks across the road. There it is! He crosses the road carefully and gives the book back. "Thank you," says the librarian. "Would you like another book?"
